summary: Chuck Berry set the template for rock and roll guitar and songwriting in the 1950s. His riffs and teenage story songs were copied by nearly every rock band that followed.
know: His first hit, Maybellene, was adapted from the fiddle tune Ida Red.
Johnny B. Goode is on the golden record carried by the Voyager spacecraft.
He was in the first class inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1986.

influencedBy.why: Berry named T-Bone Walker as a key model for his electric guitar playing and stage moves.
Berry said he identified with Louis Jordan, and the Johnny B. Goode intro echoes a guitar line from a Jordan record.
Muddy Waters sent the young Berry to Leonard Chess, which led to his Chess Records contract.
Berry cited Charlie Christian's single-note electric jazz lines as an early guitar inspiration.
Maybellene grew out of Ida Red, a fiddle tune Bob Wills and his Texas Playboys had recorded.
Berry admired Nat King Cole's clear diction and aimed to sing just as plainly.

cousins.why: Both wrote the basic song vocabulary their genres still use.
Both pack vivid little teenage stories into tight, funny verses.

summary: Little Richard was one of rock and roll's founding performers, with a pounding piano, a shrieking voice and a flamboyant stage act. His mid-1950s hits defined the music's wild side.
know: Tutti Frutti began as a bawdy song he cleaned up in the studio in 1955.
Sister Rosetta Tharpe invited him to sing at her show in Macon when he was a teenager.
The Beatles opened for him in 1962 before they were famous.

influencedBy.why: Tharpe heard him sing before her 1947 Macon concert and brought him on stage, his first time performing for a big crowd.
He named Louis Jordan as a major early influence on his jump-blues style.
He cut his hits at Cosimo Matassa's New Orleans studio with the same session players behind Fats Domino's records.

cousins.why: Both were explosive Black showmen from Georgia who made the live performance the point.
Both mixed gospel shouting with flamboyant, gender-bending style.
Both treat outrageous costume and theatrics as part of the music.

summary: Fats Domino brought New Orleans piano rhythm and blues into the early rock and roll mainstream. His relaxed rolling piano and warm voice made him one of the best-selling artists of the 1950s.
know: The Fat Man from 1949 is often called one of the first rock and roll records.
He sold more than 65 million records.
He was rescued by boat from his flooded home after Hurricane Katrina in 2005.

influencedBy.why: His nickname was given by bandleader Billy Diamond in honor of piano men like Fats Waller.
His shuffling jump-blues rhythms follow the band sound Louis Jordan made popular in the 1940s.
His 1956 hit Blueberry Hill followed Louis Armstrong's 1949 recording of the song.

cousins.why: Both are pillars of the New Orleans groove.
Both have a warm, friendly voice over a loping beat, and Jamaican ska grew partly out of New Orleans R&B.

summary: Bo Diddley built songs on a single driving rhythm, the shave-and-a-haircut pattern now called the Bo Diddley beat. His rhythm-first approach and homemade guitars shaped rock, garage and punk.
know: He built his own rectangular guitars.
He took up violin as a child before switching to guitar.
He was banned from The Ed Sullivan Show in 1955 after playing a different song than agreed.

influencedBy.why: His one-chord, rhythm-driven songs follow John Lee Hooker's boogie approach.
He named Louis Jordan among the musicians he listened to growing up.
He came up in the same South Side Chicago scene as Muddy Waters and recorded for the same Chess family of labels.

cousins.why: Both put rhythm ahead of melody and chord changes.
Both build long songs on one hypnotic groove.

summary: Elvis Presley fused country, blues and gospel at Sun Records in Memphis and became rock and roll's first superstar. His records and TV appearances brought the music to a mass audience.
know: His first single paired the blues song That's All Right with Bill Monroe's Blue Moon of Kentucky.
He was drafted into the U.S. Army in 1958 and served in West Germany.
He is the best-selling solo artist of all time by most estimates.

influencedBy.why: He recorded a sped-up version of Bill Monroe's Blue Moon of Kentucky as the B-side of his first single.
He covered Ray Charles's I Got a Woman on his first album.
He had a hit with Carl Perkins's Blue Suede Shoes in 1956.
He covered Tutti Frutti, Long Tall Sally and Rip It Up in 1956.
He recorded Blueberry Hill and called Fats Domino the real king of rock and roll.
He covered several Chuck Berry songs, including Johnny B. Goode and Promised Land.

cousins.why: Both were the defining male idol of their era.
Both became global kings of their genre and its biggest stage presence.

summary: Buddy Holly wrote, arranged and produced much of his own music in a career of under three years. His Crickets set the two-guitars, bass and drums lineup that rock bands still use.
know: He died in a plane crash on February 3, 1959, later called the day the music died.
The Beatles chose their name partly as a nod to his band, the Crickets.
He opened for Elvis Presley in Lubbock in 1955.

influencedBy.why: Seeing Elvis in Lubbock in 1955 pushed him from country toward rock and roll.
Not Fade Away is built on the Bo Diddley beat, and he recorded Diddley's song Bo Diddley.
He started out playing country songs in Hank Williams's style in the duo Buddy and Bob.
His early Buddy and Bob duo played bluegrass and western material.
He recorded Little Richard's Slippin' and Slidin' and Ready Teddy.
He recorded Chuck Berry's Brown Eyed Handsome Man.

cousins.why: Both wrote a lasting songbook in a few short years before dying young.
Both play bright, simple, catchy songs, and Weezer even wrote a hit called Buddy Holly.

summary: Jerry Lee Lewis was rock and roll's wildest piano player, pounding the keys with his hands, feet and elbows. After a 1958 scandal stalled his rock career, he reinvented himself as a country star.
know: He was the last surviving member of Sun Records' Million Dollar Quartet session.
His cousins included country singer Mickey Gilley and preacher Jimmy Swaggart.
His nickname was The Killer.
keyAlbums: Live at the Star Club, Hamburg

influencedBy.why: He idolized Hank Williams and recorded many of his songs.
He named Jimmie Rodgers as an early hero and recorded his songs.
His country boogie piano draws on the Western swing dance bands of Bob Wills's era.

cousins.why: Both are giant voices with hell-raising reputations.
Both are flamboyant piano showmen.

summary: Carl Perkins was a Sun Records rockabilly pioneer whose Blue Suede Shoes was one of the first records to top pop, country and R&B charts at once. His guitar style was a model for George Harrison and many others.
know: A car crash in 1956 kept him from promoting Blue Suede Shoes on national TV.
The Beatles recorded three of his songs.
He grew up the son of sharecroppers and learned blues from a Black field worker named John Westbrook.
songs: Everybody's Trying to Be My Baby

influencedBy.why: He said Bill Monroe's bluegrass was a major early influence on his playing.
His song Matchbox reworks Blind Lemon Jefferson's Match Box Blues.
Hearing Elvis's first Sun single convinced him to audition for Sam Phillips.

cousins.why: Both play twangy, guitar-driven country-rock built for dancing.
Both blend hillbilly twang with a rockabilly kick.

summary: Don and Phil Everly brought Appalachian close-harmony singing into rock and roll. Their two-part harmonies shaped the Beatles, Simon and Garfunkel and the Byrds.
know: Their parents Ike and Margaret Everly were country radio performers.
Bye Bye Love and Wake Up Little Susie were written by Felice and Boudleaux Bryant.
They broke up on stage in 1973 and reunited in 1983.
keyAlbums: A Date with the Everly Brothers
songs: All I Have to Do Is Dream

influencedBy.why: Their sibling harmonies come out of the bluegrass and brother-duet country tradition Bill Monroe helped define.
Their old-time family harmony singing follows the Carter Family tradition.
Don Everly said he borrowed a Bo Diddley-style rhythm for the guitar on Bye Bye Love.
They covered Little Richard's Lucille as a single in 1960.

cousins.why: Both are duos built on tight two-part harmony, and Simon and Garfunkel covered Bye Bye Love.
Both deliver pure, close country harmony singing.

summary: Eddie Cochran wrote and played teenage rock anthems with a heavy guitar sound and often overdubbed the parts himself. He died at 21 but his songs became standards for punk and hard rock bands.
know: He died after a taxi crash in England on April 17, 1960.
He performed Twenty Flight Rock in the 1956 film The Girl Can't Help It.
Paul McCartney got into the Quarrymen partly by playing Twenty Flight Rock for John Lennon.

influencedBy.why: He switched from country to rock and roll after Elvis's breakthrough in 1955 and 1956.
He released a cover of Ray Charles's Hallelujah I Love Her So in 1959.
He began in the Cochran Brothers, a country duo playing in the hillbilly style Hank Williams made famous.

cousins.why: Both made short, snarling teenage anthems, and Sid Vicious covered C'mon Everybody.
Both wrote fast, simple songs about teenage frustration.

summary: Roy Orbison sang operatic ballads of heartbreak with a huge three-octave voice. His dramatic early 1960s hits stood apart from other rock of the time.
know: He wore dark glasses after leaving his regular glasses on a plane in 1963.
He was a member of the Traveling Wilburys with Bob Dylan, George Harrison, Tom Petty and Jeff Lynne.
Oh, Pretty Woman topped the charts in both the U.S. and U.K. in 1964.

influencedBy.why: He idolized Lefty Frizzell and took the name Lefty Wilbury in his honor.
He said seeing Elvis perform in Texas in 1955 changed his sense of what was possible.
His first band, the Wink Westerners, played Western swing in Bob Wills's style.

cousins.why: Both sing towering, orchestrated heartbreak ballads.
Both build cinematic, melancholy songs around a dramatic voice.

summary: The Beatles were the most influential band of the 1960s, moving from Merseybeat hits to studio-built albums that changed what rock records could be. Lennon and McCartney's songs are among the most covered ever written.
know: They played hundreds of hours in Hamburg clubs between 1960 and 1962.
About 73 million people watched their first Ed Sullivan Show appearance in 1964.
Their last public performance was on the roof of Apple Corps in London in January 1969.
keyAlbums: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band
songs: I Want to Hold Your Hand

influencedBy.why: John Lennon said, 'Before Elvis, there was nothing.'
They took the insect idea in their name partly from Holly's Crickets and covered his Words of Love.
They covered Roll Over Beethoven and Rock and Roll Music.
McCartney modeled his screaming vocal on Long Tall Sally, and they opened for Little Richard in 1962.
They covered Matchbox, Honey Don't and Everybody's Trying to Be My Baby, and Harrison once used the stage name Carl Harrison.
Lennon and McCartney said they modeled their two-part harmonies on the Everly Brothers.
Lonnie Donegan's skiffle craze led Lennon to form the Quarrymen in 1956.
Lennon said Please Please Me began as an attempt at a Roy Orbison song.
They covered the Miracles' You've Really Got a Hold on Me.
Lennon's You've Got to Hide Your Love Away was his open attempt at a Dylan-style song.
Harrison said the riff of If I Needed Someone was based on the Byrds' The Bells of Rhymney.
McCartney said Pet Sounds was the main inspiration for Sgt. Pepper.
George Harrison studied sitar with Ravi Shankar and brought it into songs like Love You To.

cousins.why: Both reinvented their sound every year or two while staying hugely popular.
Both pushed a hit-making act into studio experiments that reset their genre.

summary: The Rolling Stones started as a blues covers band and became the longest-running major act in rock. Mick Jagger and Keith Richards built a rougher, riff-driven alternative to the Beatles.
know: They took their name from the Muddy Waters song Rollin' Stone.
Their first single was a cover of Chuck Berry's Come On.
Jagger and Richards first bonded over Chuck Berry and Muddy Waters records on a Dartford train platform in 1961.

influencedBy.why: The band took its name from Muddy Waters's song Rollin' Stone.
Their first single was Chuck Berry's Come On, and Keith Richards built his style on Berry's riffs.
They covered Mona and toured Britain with Bo Diddley in 1963.
Their cover of Little Red Rooster topped the U.K. chart, and they insisted Howlin' Wolf appear with them on Shindig! in 1965.
They covered Dixon's Little Red Rooster and I Just Want to Make Love to You.
They recorded Johnson's Love in Vain and Stop Breaking Down.
They covered Jimmy Reed's Honest I Do on their first album.
Their first U.S. single was a cover of Holly's Not Fade Away.
Brian Jones learned slide guitar from Elmore James records and briefly called himself Elmo Lewis.
Brian Jones and Jagger modeled their harmonica playing on Chicago players like Little Walter.
They covered Sam Cooke's Good Times on Out of Our Heads.
Keith Richards credited his friend Gram Parsons for the country feel of songs like Wild Horses and Dead Flowers.
Lennon and McCartney gave them I Wanna Be Your Man, their second single.

cousins.why: Both trade on rough, outlaw swagger rooted in older styles.
Both stick to raw, blues-based basics with a hard-living image.

summary: The Kinks went from the distorted power chords of You Really Got Me to Ray Davies's wry, very English story songs. They are a key link between 1960s rock, punk and Britpop.
know: Dave Davies got the distorted sound on You Really Got Me partly by slashing his amp's speaker cone.
They were effectively banned from touring the U.S. from 1965 to 1969.
The band was built around brothers Ray and Dave Davies, who often fought.
keyAlbums: The Kinks Are the Village Green Preservation Society
songs: All Day and All of the Night

influencedBy.why: Their first single was Chuck Berry's Beautiful Delilah, and they covered Too Much Monkey Business.
They covered Long Tall Sally as an early single.
They covered Bo Diddley's Cadillac on their debut album.
The Davies brothers started playing during the skiffle boom Lonnie Donegan sparked.

cousins.why: Both write sharp, very English character songs about everyday life.
Both write wry, humane story songs about ordinary people.

summary: The Who were the loudest band of the 1960s, known for Pete Townshend's windmill guitar and smashed equipment and Keith Moon's chaotic drumming. Townshend's rock operas Tommy and Quadrophenia pushed rock toward long-form storytelling.
know: Pete Townshend began smashing guitars after accidentally breaking one on a low ceiling in 1964.
Live at Leeds is often called one of the best live rock albums.
They were a favorite band of the 1960s London mod scene.

influencedBy.why: Townshend admitted he wrote I Can't Explain in imitation of the Kinks.
Their live version of Cochran's Summertime Blues was a staple of their shows.
Their debut album included covers of James Brown's I Don't Mind and Please, Please, Please.
They covered Bo Diddley's I'm a Man on My Generation.
Townshend named Steve Cropper of Booker T. and the M.G.'s as a key rhythm guitar model.
Keith Moon loved surf music, and the band covered Barbara Ann.

cousins.why: Both turned youth frustration into loud, defiant anthems.
Both are arena bands built on big, emotional rock anthems.

summary: The Yardbirds were a British blues band best known for launching three major guitarists: Eric Clapton, Jeff Beck and Jimmy Page. Their experiments with fuzz and feedback pointed toward psychedelia and hard rock.
know: Clapton left in 1965 because he thought For Your Love was too commercial.
Jimmy Page formed Led Zeppelin from the band's remains, first touring as the New Yardbirds.
They backed blues singer Sonny Boy Williamson II on a 1963 British tour.

influencedBy.why: They covered Bo Diddley's I'm a Man and Here 'Tis.
They covered Howlin' Wolf's Smokestack Lightning.
Five Live Yardbirds opens with Chuck Berry's Too Much Monkey Business.
Jeff Beck's Eastern-sounding guitar line on Heart Full of Soul copies the sitar sound Shankar brought to the West.

cousins.why: Both turn old Chicago blues into loud, raw guitar rock.
Both are guitar-led blues acts that stretch the blues with fuzz and rock volume.

summary: The Animals were a gritty British R&B band led by Eric Burdon's deep voice and Alan Price's organ. Their House of the Rising Sun was one of the first folk songs turned into a rock hit.
know: The House of the Rising Sun reached number one in both the U.K. and U.S. in 1964.
Bassist Chas Chandler later discovered and managed Jimi Hendrix.
They recorded House of the Rising Sun in a single take.
songs: The House of the Rising Sun
We Gotta Get Out of This Place

influencedBy.why: Their House of the Rising Sun followed the version on Bob Dylan's 1962 debut album.
They covered John Lee Hooker's Boom Boom.
Their hit Don't Let Me Be Misunderstood was a cover of Nina Simone's song.
Eric Burdon has called Ray Charles his greatest vocal influence, and they covered his Talkin' 'Bout You.
They covered Chuck Berry's Around and Around and Memphis, Tennessee.

cousins.why: Both are British singers who channel American R&B with a raw, deep voice.
Both play stripped-down, blues-based rock with a soulful lead voice.

summary: The Byrds invented folk rock by putting Bob Dylan's songs to electric 12-string guitar and Beatles-style harmonies. They later helped create psychedelic rock and country rock.
know: Their Mr. Tambourine Man reached number one in 1965.
Roger McGuinn bought a Rickenbacker 12-string after seeing George Harrison play one in A Hard Day's Night.
Sweetheart of the Rodeo, made with Gram Parsons, is a landmark of country rock.
songs: So You Want to Be a Rock 'n' Roll Star

influencedBy.why: Their first hit was Dylan's Mr. Tambourine Man, and they recorded many more of his songs.
McGuinn took up the electric 12-string after seeing George Harrison play one in A Hard Day's Night.
They recorded Seeger's Turn! Turn! Turn! and The Bells of Rhymney.
McGuinn said his guitar on Eight Miles High imitated John Coltrane's saxophone.
David Crosby and McGuinn introduced Indian raga ideas from Ravi Shankar's music into their playing.
Gram Parsons joined in 1968 and steered them into country on Sweetheart of the Rodeo.
Their stacked vocal harmonies draw on the Everly Brothers' sound.

cousins.why: Both built a sound on chiming, jangly guitars and folk melody.
Both pair close harmonies with folk-based songwriting.

summary: The Velvet Underground, led by Lou Reed and John Cale, wrote frank songs about drugs and street life set to drone and noise. They sold few records but became one of the most influential bands in rock.
know: Andy Warhol managed them and designed the banana cover of their first album.
Brian Eno said only about 30,000 people bought their first record, but everyone who did started a band.
Drummer Moe Tucker played standing up, often with mallets.

influencedBy.why: Lou Reed cited Ornette Coleman's free jazz as the model for his noisy guitar solos.
Moe Tucker named Bo Diddley's records as a major influence on her drumming.
Reed followed Dylan in bringing literary, street-level storytelling into rock lyrics.

cousins.why: Both were cult figures who sold modestly but became the reference point for an underground.
Both wrote unflinching songs about addiction and darkness that found their audience later.

summary: The Doors combined Jim Morrison's dark poetry with Ray Manzarek's organ and jazz-influenced players. They had no bass player on stage, with Manzarek playing bass lines on a keyboard.
know: The band took its name from Aldous Huxley's book The Doors of Perception.
Light My Fire reached number one in 1967.
Jim Morrison died in Paris in 1971 at age 27.
songs: Break On Through (To the Other Side)

influencedBy.why: They covered Howlin' Wolf's Back Door Man on their debut album.
Back Door Man, which they covered, was written by Willie Dixon.
Manzarek and Robby Krieger said the long solos on Light My Fire were modeled on Coltrane's My Favorite Things.
Morrison named Elvis as a favorite singer and an early model for his stage persona.
Morrison named Frank Sinatra among his favorite singers and borrowed his crooning phrasing.
Krieger and John Densmore studied Indian music, and its raga feel shapes songs like The End.

cousins.why: Both are poets first, with dark, literary lyrics.
Both build dark, cinematic myths of Los Angeles.

summary: Jimi Hendrix changed what the electric guitar could do with feedback, distortion and the wah pedal. In four years of fame he became the most influential rock guitarist ever.
know: He played left-handed on flipped right-handed guitars.
He played backup guitar for Little Richard and the Isley Brothers before fame.
He closed Woodstock in 1969 with a distorted version of The Star-Spangled Banner.

influencedBy.why: He covered Dylan's All Along the Watchtower and Like a Rolling Stone and said Dylan gave him the courage to sing.
He said Muddy Waters was the first guitarist he was aware of, and he reworked Muddy's Catfish Blues.
He named B.B. King as an early guitar hero.
His bends and phrasing draw heavily on Albert King, whom he watched and admired.
He opened many shows with Howlin' Wolf's Killing Floor.
He admired Buddy Guy's wild showmanship and was seen studying him at Chicago club shows.
He toured as a guitarist in Little Richard's band in 1964 and 1965.
He named Curtis Mayfield's chordal rhythm playing as a key influence on songs like Little Wing.
He played Elmore James's slide blues and cited him as an early influence.
His tricks of playing behind his head and with his teeth come from T-Bone Walker's showmanship.
He opened a London show with Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band three days after the album came out.

cousins.why: Both pushed their instrument into new, almost spiritual territory.
Both are virtuoso guitarists and showmen who fused rock, blues and funk.

summary: Cream was the first rock supergroup, with Eric Clapton, Jack Bruce and Ginger Baker. Their loud blues jams set the model for the power trio and hard rock.
know: They sold millions of records in just over two years together.
Sunshine of Your Love was written after the band saw Jimi Hendrix play.
Wheels of Fire was the first platinum-selling double album.

influencedBy.why: Their famous live Crossroads is a reworking of Johnson's Cross Road Blues.
They covered Spoonful and Sitting on Top of the World from Howlin' Wolf's repertoire.
Spoonful, a centerpiece of their shows, was written by Willie Dixon.
They covered Born Under a Bad Sign, and Clapton's Strange Brew solo borrows Albert King's phrasing.
They covered Skip James's I'm So Glad on their debut.
They recorded Rollin' and Tumblin' in the Muddy Waters style.
Jack Bruce wrote the Sunshine of Your Love riff after seeing Hendrix play in London.

cousins.why: Both are groups of star soloists who stretch songs into long improvisations.
Both are heavy British bands grounded in blues riffs.

summary: Pink Floyd began as a psychedelic band led by Syd Barrett and became masters of the concept album with Roger Waters and David Gilmour. The Dark Side of the Moon is one of the best-selling albums ever made.
know: The name combines two bluesmen, Pink Anderson and Floyd Council.
The Dark Side of the Moon spent over 900 weeks on the Billboard 200.
Syd Barrett left in 1968 after his mental health declined.
keyAlbums: The Piper at the Gates of Dawn
The Dark Side of the Moon
songs: Another Brick in the Wall, Part 2

influencedBy.why: They recorded their debut at Abbey Road while the Beatles were making Sgt. Pepper, and Nick Mason has said the Beatles shaped them.
David Gilmour learned guitar from a Pete Seeger instruction record.
Their early sets were full of R&B covers, including Bo Diddley songs.
Roger Waters has named Bob Dylan as a key influence on his lyric writing.
Gilmour has said hearing Heartbreak Hotel as a boy made him want to play.

cousins.why: Both build whole albums around a mood of isolation.
Both use texture and space as much as melody to create atmosphere.

summary: The Zombies blended jazz-tinged keyboards with soft harmonies, led by Rod Argent and singer Colin Blunstone. Their album Odessey and Oracle flopped on release but is now a classic.
know: Time of the Season became a U.S. hit in 1969 after the band had already split.
The misspelling of Odessey on the album cover was a designer's error.
They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2019.

influencedBy.why: Rod Argent said She's Not There was sparked by the title of John Lee Hooker's No One Told Me.
Argent has said Miles Davis's modal jazz shaped the chords he wrote.
They recorded Odessey and Oracle at Abbey Road right after Sgt. Pepper and used the Mellotron the Beatles had left there.

cousins.why: Both make ornate, gently orchestrated pop.
Both make dreamy, keyboard-rich psychedelic pop.

summary: Jefferson Airplane were the first San Francisco psychedelic band to break nationally. Grace Slick's voice and songs like White Rabbit became the sound of the 1967 Summer of Love.
know: They played Monterey Pop, Woodstock and Altamont.
Grace Slick joined from the Great Society and brought both Somebody to Love and White Rabbit.
Members later formed Hot Tuna and Jefferson Starship.

influencedBy.why: Grace Slick said she wrote White Rabbit's bolero build after listening to Miles Davis's Sketches of Spain.
They started as a folk group and went electric after Dylan did.
Their early folk-rock sound follows the template the Byrds set in 1965.
Paul Kantner and Marty Balin were drawn from folk toward electric rock by the Beatles' success.

cousins.why: Both are fronted by a commanding, unpredictable female singer.
Both are key psychedelic bands of the late 1960s in their own scenes.

summary: The Grateful Dead blended rock, folk, bluegrass, blues and jazz into long improvised shows. They built the biggest touring fan culture in rock, with fans called Deadheads following them for decades.
know: They allowed fans to tape their concerts.
Jerry Garcia started as a bluegrass banjo player.
They played more than 2,300 concerts.

influencedBy.why: Garcia was a bluegrass banjo player who drove across the country in 1964 to hear Bill Monroe.
Garcia cited Coltrane's long, searching solos as a model for the band's jams.
They played Johnny B. Goode and Promised Land throughout their career.
They regularly covered Haggard's Mama Tried and Sing Me Back Home.
They played dozens of Dylan songs and toured as his backing band in 1987.
Pigpen sang Jimmy Reed's Big Boss Man in their early shows.
They covered Howlin' Wolf's Smokestack Lightning.
Garcia played on Ornette Coleman's album Virgin Beauty, and Coleman sat in with the band in 1993.
Miles Davis opened for them at the Fillmore West in 1970, and his jazz-rock fed their jams.

cousins.why: Both are road-warrior acts with a devoted, family-like fan culture.
Both stretch songs into long, open-ended grooves on stage.

summary: Janis Joplin was the first female rock superstar, singing blues and soul with raw power. Her performances with Big Brother and the Holding Company made her a 1960s icon.
know: Her breakthrough came at the Monterey Pop Festival in 1967.
She paid for a headstone for Bessie Smith's unmarked grave in 1970.
Me and Bobby McGee became a number one hit after her death.
keyAlbums: I Got Dem Ol' Kozmic Blues Again Mama!

influencedBy.why: She named Bessie Smith as a key influence and helped pay for her headstone.
She said hearing Lead Belly records as a teenager pulled her toward the blues.
She modeled her early folk singing on Odetta.
She cited Otis Redding's stage intensity as a model after seeing him at Monterey.

cousins.why: Both sang raw, wounded soul and blues, and both died at 27.
Both are fierce, uncompromising female rock voices.

summary: Creedence Clearwater Revival, led by John Fogerty, played tight, short songs steeped in Southern rock and roll and blues. They had a run of hits from 1969 to 1971 and played Woodstock.
know: Despite their swampy Southern sound, they came from the San Francisco Bay Area.
They had five number two singles in the U.S. but never a number one.
They released three albums in 1969 alone.
songs: Have You Ever Seen the Rain

influencedBy.why: John Fogerty has called Carl Perkins and the Sun rockabilly sound a key model.
They covered Good Golly, Miss Molly on Bayou Country.
They covered Bo Diddley's Before You Accuse Me on Cosmo's Factory.
Fogerty said Booker T. and the M.G.'s were his model of a perfect band.
They recorded Midnight Special and Cotton Fields, two songs associated with Lead Belly.
Fogerty name-checked Buck Owens in Lookin' Out My Back Door.

cousins.why: Both write plain, working-class songs with a rhythmic drive.
Both write grounded Southern story songs about class and war.

summary: Santana, led by guitarist Carlos Santana, fused rock and blues with Afro-Cuban percussion. The band broke through at Woodstock and returned to the top with Supernatural in 1999.
know: Their Woodstock set came before their debut album was released.
Supernatural won nine Grammy Awards.
Carlos Santana was born in Autlán, Mexico.

influencedBy.why: Their hit Oye Como Va is a cover of Tito Puente's song.
Carlos Santana named B.B. King as the guitarist who made him want to play.
Santana called Coltrane's A Love Supreme a spiritual guide and recorded a version on Love Devotion Surrender.
Carlos has said Miles Davis's Bitches Brew era shaped Santana's jazz-rock turn.
Black Magic Woman was written by Peter Green of Fleetwood Mac.
Carlos called John Lee Hooker a mentor and recorded The Healer with him.

cousins.why: Both play long, spiritual solos over rhythmic grooves.
Both have a singing, instantly recognizable guitar tone.

summary: Led Zeppelin took British blues to new extremes of volume and power and mixed in folk and Eastern sounds. They were the biggest rock band of the 1970s and a foundation of heavy metal.
know: They started as the New Yardbirds after Jimmy Page's old band split.
Led Zeppelin IV has no title on its cover.
They split after drummer John Bonham died in 1980.

influencedBy.why: They covered Dixon's You Shook Me and I Can't Quit You Baby, and Whole Lotta Love later credited Dixon after a lawsuit.
Their You Shook Me follows Muddy Waters's 1962 recording.
The Lemon Song and Travelling Riverside Blues borrow lines from Robert Johnson.
The Lemon Song now credits Howlin' Wolf because it reworks his Killing Floor.
Robert Plant idolized Elvis and met him in 1974.
Page based Babe I'm Gonna Leave You on Joan Baez's recording of the song.
Jimmy Page formed the band out of the Yardbirds, and they first toured as the New Yardbirds.
John Bonham's drum intro to Rock and Roll was adapted from Little Richard's Keep A-Knockin'.
They played Eddie Cochran's Somethin' Else and C'mon Everybody on stage.
The Crunge is a deliberate tribute to James Brown's funk.
Plant wrote Going to California with Joni Mitchell in mind and named her as an influence.
Gallows Pole is an old folk song best known from Lead Belly's recording.

cousins.why: Both mined old blues and R&B records for heavy riffs, and the Beastie Boys looped Bonham's When the Levee Breaks drums.
Both turn Delta blues into huge, stripped-back riff rock.

summary: King Crimson, led by guitarist Robert Fripp, helped define progressive rock with their 1969 debut. Through many lineups they kept moving into jazz, metal, minimalism and new wave.

summary: Greta Van Fleet are a Michigan band of three Kiszka brothers and a friend whose 1970s-style hard rock made them stars in their teens. Their sound is widely compared to Led Zeppelin.
know: The band is named after Gretna Van Fleet, an elder of their hometown.
They won the Grammy for Best Rock Album in 2019 for From the Fires.
Josh, Jake and Sam Kiszka are brothers; Josh and Jake are twins.

influencedBy.why: Robert Plant joked in 2018 that they 'are Led Zeppelin I,' and their riffs and Josh Kiszka's wail closely follow Zeppelin.

cousins.why: Both are young acts reviving a classic sound.
